why: PyROOT turns a Python set literal into a RooArgSet in the set's iteration order, which follows the wrapped objects' addresses and so differs run to run - the harness's own sandbox names differ in length from run to run, and so does the layout. For the tutorials listed here ROOT itself therefore has more than one output, and the cached oracle holds only one draw of the coin. Each entry is a whole unchanged tutorial run by the same ROOT the oracle is; the harness accepts xrdroot only when it matches a ROOT output exactly: the cached draw or one of these, never anything else.
